title: Branching and Step Sequences
statement: Let $n,l,pos,pos'$ be natural numbers, let $c$ be an initial configuration, let $m$ be a memory function, and let $v$ be an integer. Suppose that $n$ steps of the program take $c$ to the configuration with memory $m$ and program counter $l$ if $v<0$, and with memory $m$ and program counter $pos$ otherwise. If a proposition $p$ is equivalent to $v\ge 0$ and $pos=pos'$, then if $p$ holds, $n$ steps take $c$ to the configuration with memory $m$ and program counter $pos'$; if $p$ fails, they take $c$ to the configuration with memory $m$ and program counter $l$.
hypotheses_covered: There is an $n$-step execution from $c$ to the configuration with memory $m$ and program counter $l$ when $v<0$, or $pos$ otherwise
The program counters $pos$ and $pos'$ are equal
